items.title: The 'hands-off' doctrine in election disputes: A case for reconsideration
items.summary: Democracy, as the Supreme Court has repeatedly reminded us, is not merely an incident of our constitutional scheme, but a part of its basic structure. In Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu , the Supreme Court held that ‘democracy’ and ‘free and fair elections’ are inseparable twins. In Rajbala v. State of Haryana , the Supreme Court described the right to vote and right to contest in elections to local bodies as constitutional rights. Earlier, in Jyoti Basu v. Debi Ghosal , the Supreme Court held that the said right is neither a fundamental right nor a common law right, but a statutory right. Rajbala reads it to constitutional rank at least in elections to panchayats. Nothing in this article turns on winning that classificatory battle. Constitutional right or statutory right, the interest at stake is the same and the Court’s own basic structure jurisprudence has already told us how much it weighs. Yet, when disputes touching upon the electoral process are actually brought before the constitutional courts, a curious reluctance sets in. items.title: Arundhati Roy: ‘Message from Jantar Mantar is bigger than electoral defeat’
items.summary: In a wide-ranging interview with Newslaundry , Arundhati Roy discusses her new book, My Mother, My Gangster , which draws on the story of her mother, Mary Roy, to explore her own childhood, family, relationships, and journey to becoming a writer. The conversation, however, went beyond the book to address contemporary politics and student movements as well. Roy spoke at length about leaving home at 16, studying architecture in Delhi, her friendships, and the early days of her writing career. She describes her mother as a woman who was both “extraordinary” and “extremely harsh”, and explains why it’s essential to see her not merely as a mother, but as an independent woman in her own right. The conversation then proceeded to the recent student protests at Jantar Mantar, the state of the education system, Hindutva politics, elections, democratic institutions, the movements in Narmada and Bastar, the environment, and social inequality. Roy argues that the current student movement can’t be understood merely through the lens of exams and education. Watch the full conversation. Small teams can do great things. items.summary: Actor Prakash Raj, on Tuesday, August 11, has alleged that his name has been removed from the voter list in Bengaluru during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Karnataka. The actor’s name has been included in the ASDDO (Absent, Shifted Address, Dead, Duplicate and Others) category. The move comes amid a separate court case in which he faces allegations of being enrolled in multiple electoral rolls in Karnataka and Telangana. Prakash Raj, a vocal critic of alleged irregularities in voter rolls, said that he wanted to share a “joke”, and added that he was among 65 lakh voters whose votes had been deleted. Emphasising his connection to the area, the actor said he was born, raised and educated there and began his theatre career in the constituency. items.title: Can social media platforms suspend accounts based on copyright strikes? Delhi High Court to examine
items.summary: The Delhi High Court is set to examine whether social media platforms can suspend or delete accounts based on copyright strikes. Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani today framed this preliminary issue, which would be considered by the Court. “Whether the system of suspension and subsequent deletion or takedown of the account on the social media platform based on the system of copyright strikes by social media platforms, amounts to a violation of the principles laid down in Shreya Singhal and MySpace judgments?” Meta, Google and Telegram have been directed to specifically address this issue in their replies to the suit and interim injunction application. The case will be heard next on September 24. Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani The Court passed the order while dealing with a suit filed by a digital content creator Saurabh Maurya operating under the name “IITian Trader”. Maurya moved the Court challenging the suspension of his Instagram account by Meta due to fake copyright strikes on his posts. He is also seeking compensation from persons running an extortion racket by abusing Meta’s copyright enforcement mechanism. Senior advocate Diya Kapur and advocate Nakul Gandhi appeared for Maurya

items.title: Rule mandating uniform healthcare rates constitutionally valid: Centre tells Supreme Court
items.summary: The Centre has told the Supreme Court that a rule requiring private hospitals to charge within a government-determined range of rates for medical procedures is constitutionally valid, even as it conceded that the range itself has not yet been finalised due to a lack of consensus among states. The submission came in a counter affidavit filed by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in response to a petition filed by the All India Ophthalmological Society (petitioner) challenging Rule 9(ii) of the Clinical Establishments (Central Government) Rules, 2012. The rule requires hospitals to charge within a range of rates fixed by the Centre in consultation with States. The petitioner had argued that specialists providing medical procedures in metropolitan cities could not be expected to charge the same rates as those practising in smaller towns and remote areas. The petition first came up before the Supreme Court in April 2024 when a Bench of Justices Sudhanshu Dhulia and Prasanna B Varale had flagged that private hospitals often get land at subsidised rates on the condition that they reserve a share of beds for poorer patients.
